plugins.name: personal-defaults
plugins.description: Fabrizio's always-on personal conventions as one install — a dependency-only bundle carrying git-conventions, contributor-workflow, session-workflow, upstream-research, and scaffolding. Contributes no skills of its own.

plugins.name: git-conventions
plugins.description: Standing git/PR hygiene conventions (Conventional Commits, linear history, squash-vs-rebase, no fixup commits, force-push policy, and which commit signature warnings to ignore).

plugins.name: contributor-workflow
plugins.description: Personal contributor/review workflow commands (currently /ready-to-merge); depends on git-conventions.

plugins.name: docs-standards
plugins.description: Repo-adopted documentation conventions — Diátaxis docs, Nygard ADRs, ephemeral-plan lifecycle, README-index and staleness discipline, agent/verify callouts, and a session-end doc-maintenance checklist hook. Depends on markdown-standards.

plugins.name: claude-code-web
plugins.description: Working preferences and hard constraints for Claude Code Web — the egress proxy and CA bundle, GitHub-via-MCP, containers replaced across idle periods, repo scoping and add_repo's cross-owner rule, project config in a multi-repo session, why repo-adopted plugins never load and how user-scope ones arrive, and delegating unrunnable steps to CI. Environment-agnostic.

plugins.name: personal-cloud-environment
plugins.description: The record of Fabrizio's own Claude Code Web environment — its network allowlist, environment variables, and setup — as manually applied on top of the platform defaults, plus the round-trip rule that keeps that record and the live environment in step. Installing it also brings in what that environment carries: claude-code-web and the personal-defaults bundle.

plugins.name: upstream-research
plugins.description: Researching and verifying facts about third-party/upstream components — go to the authoritative source (the project's own repo and docs), distrust training data, web-search summaries, and generated docs, and record provenance.

plugins.name: terraform-standards
plugins.description: Conventions for a Terraform/HCL configuration repo — one .tf per concern, resource names that mirror the real object, sensitive values as variables, durations as arithmetic, pinned providers with a committed lock, and adopting existing resources via import blocks.

plugins.name: terraform-provider-standards
plugins.description: Conventions for building a Terraform provider in Go — the terraform-plugin-framework layout, tfplugindocs-generated docs, MPL-2.0 per-file license headers, and adopting the shared flungo/github-workflows provider CI (golangci-lint v2, GoReleaser dual-registry release).

plugins.name: markdown-standards
plugins.description: Markdown authoring conventions — unambiguous cross-references and link hygiene, semantic line breaks, unique cross-referenced headings, adjacent-blockquote handling, compact tables (delimiter rows included), handling lint rules a linter bump introduces, fix-the-target-never-suppress remediation for markdownlint/link-check failures, and the /adopt-markdown-ci onboarding command.

plugins.name: session-workflow
plugins.description: Named commands for ending a Claude session well — /session-clean to confirm nothing durable is left only in the chat, and /handoff to carry an unfinished session into a fresh one.

plugins.name: scaffolding
plugins.description: Setting up, building out, and extending repos across the fleet — gated on verified ownership (an owned repo adopts the conventions and standards plugins; a fork or third-party repo gets nothing without explicit consent), routing to the shared CI and the helper repos (github-workflows, claude-plugins, terraform-github) added as needed.
